notes: Uses the pinned Pith coding-agent SDK directly (CreateAgentSession, SessionManager, RunPolicy, GenerateSummary) instead of the TypeScript wrapper around Pi. The verify_candidate tool is registered through codingagent.NewToolRegistry, and Pi JavaScript extensions are deliberately not executed; equivalent behavior must be supplied as Go tools or ToolHooks.

Filesystem walking, hashing, sorting and strongly connected components are native Go. AST traversal and module resolution run against the embedded TypeScript 5.9.3 compiler executed with Goja through small bridge snippets; this is not a Go reimplementation of the compiler.

The command surface, flags, defaults, numeric validation, JSON projections and exit codes are preserved. Console writes become Main(ctx, args, stdout, stderr) return codes; signal cancellation and os.Exit move to cmd/portsmith/main.go so Main stays testable in-process.

The upstream script was an offline replay of the bundled examples/event-stream tree. The Go repository does not bundle that tree, so DemoTask exposes the same replay as a library helper that takes an example directory with source/ and reference-go/. docs/USAGE.md documents the workflow.

The reviewed oracle cases and Go judge text are kept as fixtures. Running the original TypeScript case driver uses the embedded TypeScript compiler plus Goja instead of tsx, so no Node or second Portsmith process is spawned.

Version-1 plan execution, the transactional per-unit commit journal and Git recovery are Go. The Go verifier identity is portsmith-native-go-v1, so receipts written by the TypeScript verifier are treated as stale and re-verified.
Reads PORTSMITH_* then OMNI_* environment variables and Pith's catalog capacities. API keys are never logged or serialized (ModelConfig.APIKey is json:"-").
Version-2 batch/module workflow is Go, including needs-preparation preflight, additive baselines, per-module commits and recovery from the resumable journal.
The worker thread that evaluated the TypeScript source oracle is replaced by in-process execution with the embedded TypeScript compiler and Goja; there is no worker thread or subprocess.

Process-group setup and kill are split into process_unix.go and process_windows.go so the binary cross-compiles with CGO disabled. Go and Git remain external development tools; they are never bundled.

Isolated candidate copies, gofmt, compile, vet, candidate tests, frozen judge tests and fingerprint-bound receipts are Go. VERIFIER_VERSION is portsmith-native-go-v1 rather than the TypeScript verifier id.
